title: A practical guide to content models
content:
Content models are the quiet contract between your editor, your template and your build output. A small, consistent model makes every other part of the site easier to maintain.

Posts and pages

Posts are chronological. They carry labels, excerpts and comments, and they generate dated routes. Pages are evergreen. They use short /p/ routes and intentionally avoid post-only fields.

Fields that matter

  • slug controls the public URL and should stay readable.
  • status decides whether content appears in public output.
  • publishAt supports scheduled publishing without changing files manually.

Keep the model boring

Resist adding fields that the template never reads. A boring model is easy to validate, easy to migrate and easy to explain to the next person who edits the site.
excerpt: Understand the difference between posts, pages and the fields that drive public routes.
